author: Ifmyante
text:
I'm gonna take a leaf from Rufus' journal and post a poem.

I wrote it some time ago, while quite poor. Reading it now, I'm glad I did!

Nevermore

I hear the distant echo

of a song I knew before,

it hovers o'er the river

I swam in days of yore,

when enclosed me only sunshine

and all the world was mine,

'fore penury got its grip on me

in the dark'ning veil of time

I hear the distant echo

of a song I knew before,

it plays in attic treasure chests

my mind loved to explore,

when diamond chips and pirate ships

abounded on the main,

'fore my childhood dreams cried mutiny

now no mystery remains

I hear the distant echo

of a song I knew before,

it swings on oak tree pendulums

I tied before the war

'tween a young boy's dreams of flying

and an old man's hopes of dying,

and with time's speed multiplying

'til the clock tic tocs no more

I hear the distant echo

of a song I knew before,

so I'll ramble on

and sing my song

and regard not nevermore

Super poem If ...Thank you, Thank you.

Just grabs your heart right from the first line.

All of our life that we have enjoyed or suffered through enters into how
 we trade today. How many times did RED say in the PIE thread "trading
will match our personality".

I have started thinking of the chart as a mirror to your personality.
Certain times you trade it just fine when you are understanding what is
seen in the mirror. Other times it is like reading a book in the mirror,
 all is backward. Everything you do is wrong. The personality is still
there but in those cases we have not learned what it takes to "Flip the
 print". To "flip the print" might be something as simple as
understanding a Quasimodo :)

author: Ifmyante
text:
oneday wrote: At the risk of being flamed...will this not need a little editing?...

"We won't charge for these lessons; we intend to give them all for
free. It is my intention (Hi, I'm Ifmyante, by the way) to write the
most comprehensive and no BS Wiki course on trading that has ever been
written, and put it in the site for free."

Flamed? Not at all! I'm delighted this came up in such a polite and considerate manner :)

The article doesn't need editing at all.

RTM has the most comprehensive and no BS Wiki course on trading that has ever been written, and it's all on the site for free!

The paid course is a luxury rather than a necessity. Anybody who puts in
 the work to make the free lessons their own, has just as much chance of
 making it as those who pay for the course. The course is just a
shortcut. No more, no less.

It was implicit that the first rung of RTM was all about reading the
market. Learning to trade it was to be a personal journey, aided by
seniors as one climbs the ladder. But there'll be a module on the course
 dedicated to trading, and making trade plans to suit each lifestyle and
 personality. So yes, in this case, there IS a difference.

It may seem that I started RTM for altruistic reasons, but that's not
the case. Sure, I stop to help people who've broken down or are in some
other trouble, but I do that because it makes ME feel good. I started
RTM to make an army of great traders who'll work with me in the future.
No altruism there. I'm delighted I did, as we already have our first
fund traders lined up and ready to go.

So why don't I now hand out ALL I know for free to everybody? I steal
orders from the big institutions, but not so many that they lose out.
The more people I tell how to do this, the more of their orders will be
taken. Once they can't get their orders filled, they'll need to change
their methods - methods that have been very secret for a very long time.
 This would render the information I have sold obsolete.

I'm so proud that so many have earned the keys to the kingdom through
hard work and perseverance. To then just give the keys away would be
truly irresponsible.

So, in essence, this course will be a luxury, absolutely not a necessity!
